the three-state Markov and dynamic linear models are the most promising for short- and long-term forecasting respectively.

the models under investigation are advantageous in different contexts and that the three-state Markov approach is the most reliable for forecasting the short-term evolution of epidemics in the meningitis belt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system for forecasting district level weekly incidence in the meningitis belt.
the development of an integrated system that can provide both early warnings of epidemics and predictions of epidemic magnitude, and which is capable of being used in the meningitis belt countries.
the development of a spatiotemporel early warning system to aid the control of meningococcal disease in sub-Saharan Africa and we report progress towards the achievement of this goal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three-state Markov and the dynamic linear model should both be used as components of an early warning and response system.
the best model for predicting meningitis epidemics is one which combines both the Markov model and the dynamic linear model.
, depending on the purpose, different modelling approaches may be used to provide reliable short-term forecasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the models considered are useful for predicting meningitis epidemics in different ways.

we have demonstrated that the use of a simple statistical model to predict weekly incidence in districts in the meningitis belt is feasible and that the predictions are useful in a variety of situations.
the dynamic linear model is the best model to use in a forecasting context.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of forecasting model is highly dependent on the application context, and we recommend that a suite of models be developed to provide the most accurate and reliable forecasting for a given situation.
